result: {"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the lower tail lobe (stroke 4), one of the two lobes that give the fish its forked tail, which is the feature that makes the outline read as a fish rather than a blob. The table's picture stands at 115 of 115 dominoes connected to the start, and my lobe is part of that fully connected run. Execution: I laid the lobe in short, steady batches of two or three dominoes, carrying it on from the bottom line where Tom's run ended near the join. Once it was down I inspected the join closely and found nothing needing repair, so I kept my hands off to avoid bumping the table. Collaboration: I confirmed my assignment out loud, told the table I would wait for the bottom line to reach my lobe, and gave updates as I progressed so Tom and Maya knew when to stay clear and when to check the tail. I kept communication short and specific, which helped the group stay coordinated while four people worked in the same region. Leadership: I took ownership of a defined piece and carried it through to completion without needing to be chased. I also checked my own join before calling it done, and then stepped back at the right moment to protect the finished work.
